paper.title: Online Learning for Function Placement in Serverless Computing

settings.name_in_paper: Virtual Function Placement (VFP) with stochastic costs and average resource constraints
unmapped: Arms are N computation nodes (canonical K); contexts are M i.i.d. function classes (M_ctx) with unknown arrival distribution lambda, including a null class
K_res resource types with known capacities beta_{i,k}; average resource constraints (sum_j lambda_j p_{i,j} a_{i,j,k}/beta_{i,k} <= 1) must hold with high probability
Resource requirements A_{i,j,k}(t) in [0,1] observed for all nodes after arrival (before placement); only the cost of the chosen node is observed
Comparator is the optimal static randomized placement policy solving a known-parameter LP; a fictitious reject node with infinite capacity and cost 1 ensures feasibility
settings.definition_quote: We assume that placing a function of class~$j$ in node~$i$ has cost~$C_{i,j}$ ... for all $i,j$, $(C_{i,j}(t))_{t \ge 0}$ is i.i.d. with mean $c_{i,j} \in [0,1]$ ... $(A_{i,j,k}(t))_{t \ge 0}$ is i.i.d. with mean $a_{i,j,k} \in [0,1]$ ... $(j(t))_{t\ge0}$ is i.i.d. with distribution $\lambda$. R(T) = \sum_{t=1}^T \mathbb{E}(f({\hat p}(t),c,\lambda) - f(p^\star,c,\lambda))

algorithms.name: Fast algorithm (base algorithm with geometric update times rho^k)

symbols.M_ctx: number of function classes M (contexts, including null class)

conditions: a fictitious reject node with infinite capacity and cost 1 is included

source.label: th:regret
source.quote: Under the proposed algorithm the constraints are satisfied with high probability and the regret per unit of time vanishes at the rate: {R(T) \over T} \le {N M \over T} [ 2( \sqrt{2} + 1) \sqrt{T \ln T} + 6 K (1 + \ln T) ] \underset{T \to \infty}{\sim} O( N M \sqrt{\ln T \over T } )

results.notes: Stated as per-round regret R(T)/T; multiplied by T. Paper's N (nodes) mapped to canonical K (arms); paper's K renamed K_res. Regret defined via expected mean costs of the policy, so pseudo-regret against best static policy. Algorithm uses ln t, so anytime.

bound.expression_latex: \mathbb{P} (\max_{i,k} g_{i,k}({\hat p}(t)) \le 1) \ge 1 - 6 N M K {\ln T \over T}

source.label: th:regret
source.quote: \mathbb{P} (\max_{i,k} g_{i,k}({\hat p}(t)) \le 1) \ge 1 - 6 N M K {\ln T \over T}\underset{T \to \infty}{\to} 1

results.notes: Bound on probability that the selected policy violates the average resource constraints. Statement mixes t and T; the proof gives 6NMK/t per round. Recorded as violation probability.
